replay.note: The overlay test/parity/server-overlay.json declares port 3010 and both passes were captured on it. Absolute Location headers embed the port and replay.js does not normalize an origin, so a replay on another port needs a corpus captured there.

applicationHead.note: The HEAD each pass records is the commit the application was read from when it ran, and it is necessarily the parent of the commit that carries this evidence: a replay cannot run against a commit that does not exist until the replay has finished. What matters is that the application source is the same in both. Checkable: `git diff --name-only 0716cd2..HEAD` lists only test/parity/corpus.json, test/parity/corpus.json.provenance.json, test/parity/corpus.secure.json and test/parity/corpus.secure.json.provenance.json - four data files no application module requires - so no application behaviour changed between the recorded HEAD and the delivered one.

verification.note: What was run against this corpus, and what it reported. The result and report artifacts are not committed: replay.js's output-path contract is owned outside this artifact, and writing generated evidence into the source tree is the very thing that contract is being tightened about. The commands below reproduce both runs.

selfConsistency.what: replay of this corpus against the tree it was captured from. The strictest mode: every difference fails and the approved deviation must NOT materialize. A corpus that cannot replay against its own tree is nondeterministic, and this is where that shows.
selfConsistency.command: node test/parity/replay.js --app <worktree at 2f8712a> --corpus test/parity/corpus.json --secure-corpus test/parity/corpus.secure.json --pass both --self-check --node-flags "--pending-deprecation --trace-deprecation"

selfConsistency.reading: Every scenario that can be driven drove, every driven scenario had a recorded baseline to compare against, and the one scenario that is not driven is auth.outcome.lookup-error, which carries an unreachableReason rather than a record. The differences that remain are the five generated-value classes the corpus enumerates under `residualVolatility`, and they are why this run does not exit 0: they close in replay.js's volatile set and in test/parity/seed.js, neither of which is this artifact. The one failing named check is the zero-warning condition, which fails against the BASE COMMIT for the base commit's own reasons: iconv-lite's DEP0005 through nodemailer 2.7.2, and Mongoose's strictQuery notice. Both are fixed in the migrated tree.

approvedDeviations.baseline: The request never settles: the image branch ends at `.bytes(...)` with no `return` and nothing that resolves the deferred [lib/controllers/files.js:98-100], so the step is recorded as an expected timeout.

approvedDeviations.reason: An unsettled request is the absence of a response, not a behaviour a client can depend on, so R-d's protection does not attach to it; the intended response is present in the same function for the non-image case; and R-b is unqualified about routes serving.

againstTheMigratedTree.reading: The approved deviation materialized in BOTH passes and was reported as an approved change - outcome "timed-out" -> "answered" on the image branch of the file download - which is the outcome AAP 0.7 authorizes. The remaining unapproved differences are two classes, neither of them a property of this artifact: the five generated-value classes enumerated under `residualVolatility`, and a session-cookie emission difference on six routes where the baseline re-emitted `session=...; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/` and the target sends no Set-Cookie at all - GET /account/{accountPage}, DELETE /api/folders/{folderId}, PUT /api/folders/{folderId}/name, DELETE /api/users, POST /admin/upload and POST /api/admin/featured-course. That second class is a real target behaviour difference this corpus exists to surface, and it belongs to whoever owns the session and controller conversions. The zero-warning check fails on one line: the pre-existing DEP0005 from compress-commons via archiver 2.1.1, raised at module scope.
